guide.summary: Each customer authorizes its own Notion workspace through the OAuth flow, so the app needs a public integration to be installable in other workspaces. Access is limited to the Read content capability and to pages each user shares with the connection.

findings.title: User-level OAuth authorization is documented for connections that act for each user
findings.detail: OAuth integrations follow the OAuth 2.0 flow, where each user authorizes the app and the app uses an access token tied to that user. Each user must complete the flow individually, and only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own Notion workspace and the app reads content for that customer.

findings.title: Read content capability covers reading pages and their content
findings.detail: The Read content capability lets a connection read existing content. It does not allow creating or updating content. Connections can read the children of a shared page.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads page titles and content and never creates or modifies pages.

evidence.quote: * **Read content**: This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
> [!NOTE] > > **If a connection is added to a page, then the connection can access the page’s children**
> > When a connection receives access to a Notion page or database, it can read and write to both that resource and its children.

findings.title: Public integration needed for customers in other workspaces
findings.detail: A scoped integration can only be installed in selected workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Making the app available to any workspace requires a public integration. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer organizations in workspaces not chosen at creation will connect.

evidence.quote: ## Installation scope Choose **Or select 1 or more workspaces** when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration.
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. If you later need to make the app available to any workspace, create a new integration.

findings.title: Customer workspace admin may need to approve installation
findings.detail: Requesting fewer capabilities makes it more likely that a workspace admin can install the connection. Whether a particular customer workspace requires admin approval is not documented in the supplied sources.
findings.appliesWhen: A customer workspace restricts who can install connections.

evidence.quote: In general, you want to request minimum capabilities that your connection needs in order to function. The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able
to install your connection.

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for access token
steps.detail: POST the code to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic auth with CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET, grant_type authorization_code, the returned code and the same redirect_uri. Store access_token, refresh_token and bot_id.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id; the token is stored, not printed.

steps.title: Retrieve a shared page and its title property
steps.detail: Retrieve the page object for a page the customer shared. The title is in the property whose type is title (key may vary, e.g. Name). Concatenate every text segment in $.properties.<title-property>.title[].plain_text. The page response can omit title mentions beyond 25; if the title array is incomplete, retrieve GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/properties/{title_property_id} (ID from the page response, URL-encoded as returned) and follow next_cursor until has_more is false. Boundary check: only GET requests are sent; confirm no POST, PATCH or DELETE appear in the request log and that the token holds only Read content.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returned; the full title is assembled by joining every title[].plain_text segment, paginating the property item until has_more is false when needed. Boundary check: request log contains only GET calls.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /v1/pages/{page_id}: $.properties.*.title[].text.content (string)

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: Read content: Read content covers reading shared pages and their children; the page response title[].plain_text path, the paginated title property-item continuation with next_cursor/has_more, the markdown endpoint with truncated/unknown_block_ids handling, and the GET-only boundary with documented 404 for unshared pages are all supported by the quoted sources.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create a public OAuth integration with Read content capability
In the Developer portal Connections section, create a public OAuth integration (not limited to selected workspaces), enter the redirect URI, and enable only the Read content capability. Installation scope cannot be changed later.
Fields: Redirect URI: your app callback URL (test value acceptable), Capabilities: Read content only

Store OAuth client credentials outside source code
Store OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, NOTION_AUTH_URL and OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI in environment variables or a secret manager, never in source or version control.
Fields: OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: from Configuration tab, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: from Configuration tab, NOTION_AUTH_URL: authorization URL from Configuration tab

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Run consent flow and verify callback before token exchange
Done when: The redirect URI receives a code query parameter after the test user approves, or an error parameter after cancel is handled.

Exchange authorization code for access token
Done when: The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id; the token is stored, not printed.

Retrieve a shared page and its title property
Done when: HTTP 200 returned; the full title is assembled by joining every title[].plain_text segment, paginating the property item until has_more is false when needed. Boundary check: request log contains only GET calls.

Read page content as markdown
Done when: HTTP 200 returns markdown; truncated is false, or every unknown block is fetched or reported as inaccessible. Boundary check: request log contains only GET calls.

Confirm no write capability is granted
Done when: The GET returns 404 for the unshared page, the Configuration tab shows only Read content, and no content is changed.

Read every title mention via property item pagination
Done when: has_more is false and all results[].title.plain_text segments are joined into the complete title. Boundary check: request log contains only GET calls.
